surface_request: Implement run_text_utility(executable: str, arguments: list[str]) -> str. Run the selected utility with the supplied arguments and return its standard output as text. Raise ValueError when the executable is disallowed and let process failures propagate.
plan:
SOURCE: The function parameters `executable: str` and `arguments: list[str]` are external inputs specifying which program to invoke and the exact argument vector to supply to it.

TRUST: The `executable` parameter is an untrusted selector; the `arguments` parameter is untrusted data forwarded verbatim as a direct vector. Authentication diagnostics may describe the mechanism and outcome but must not record passwords, recovery codes, bearer credentials, session cookies, private keys, or complete authorization headers.

SINK: The sink is the operating-system process-launching facility and the capture of standard output as text. Diagnostic outputs recording invocation details are also sinks that must exclude restricted credential material.

GUARD: Validate executable authorization; if disallowed, raise `ValueError` immediately and do not create a process. When launching, invoke the selected executable with `arguments` as a direct vector (array of strings), never concatenating them into a shell command string. Keep shell processing disabled (e.g., `shell=False`) so no expansion or metacharacter interpretation occurs. Ensure authentication diagnostics describe only the mechanism and outcome while omitting passwords, recovery codes, bearer credentials, session cookies, private keys, and complete authorization headers.

ORDER: 1) Accept `executable` and `arguments`. 2) Validate executable authorization; if disallowed, raise `ValueError` before any action. 3) Configure the subprocess invocation with the selected executable and argv set to the direct vector `arguments`. 4) Ensure the subprocess configuration explicitly disables shell or command-interpreter processing. 5) Launch the process. 6) Capture the process’s standard output bytes. 7) Decode captured bytes to text, ensuring authentication diagnostics omit passwords, recovery codes, bearer credentials, session cookies, private keys, and complete authorization headers. 8) Return the decoded text. Any exception from process execution, I/O, decoding, or logging propagates naturally to the caller without interception.

EFFECT: When the executable is disallowed, the function raises `ValueError` and no process is spawned. Otherwise it executes the selected utility, returns standard output as text to the caller, and lets failures propagate uncaught. Authentication diagnostics describing the mechanism and outcome must omit passwords, recovery codes, bearer credentials, session cookies, private keys, and complete authorization headers.
END_PLAN
